scenario: WIBTA if I don't let my friends stay in my hotel room after a rave. | My boyfriend and I are going to LED USA next month and I got us a hotel room to stay in that night. We live in the same city as the rave, but we both decided that neither of us would be up to driving home that night (30 minute drive + general post-rave hectic-ness) and our hotel is less than a 10 minute walk from the venue. It's just one of those nights where we want to spend some time away from home too. My friends (not super close, but we've been cool in the past) are from about 2 hours away. They didn't book a hotel room early because they were banking on sharing a hotel room with some other friends, but that fell through. Now the hotel prices are kind of getting expensive, so they asked if I would let them stay in my room and split the cost. I told them "No, I booked it so I could chill with and fuck my boyfriend later that night." Now they're calling me selfish for not letting them stay in my room, telling me how much of a waste it is for me to spend money when I could just go home when they don't have the choice. My boyfriend is leaving the decision of letting them stay or not up to me since I paid for the hotel room. WIBTA if I didn't let them stay?

First, I booked the hotel room because my boyfriend and I wanted to have a nice night out without worrying about driving home. It's a 30-minute drive, and after a rave, we both thought it would be safer and less stressful to stay in the hotel. Plus, it's only a 10-minute walk from the venue, which is convenient. Now, my friends from two hours away didn't book a hotel early because they were hoping to share a room with someone else, but that fell through. Now, hotel prices are high, and they're asking if they can stay in my room and split the cost. I said no because I booked it to chill with my boyfriend and maybe have some alone time with him. They're calling me selfish for not letting them stay, and they're saying it's a waste of money for me to spend on the hotel when I could just go home. But I don't feel like going home, and they don't have that choice because they're from out of town. My boyfriend is leaving the decision up to me since I paid for the hotel. So, I need to decide whether it's right or wrong to not let them stay. Hmm, so on one hand, I booked the room for a reasonâĢĶto have a nice, stress-free night with my boyfriend. On the other hand, my friends are in a tough spot because they didn't book early and now they're stuck without a place to stay. They're also saying it's a waste of money for me to spend on the hotel when I could just go home. But wait, I don't want to go home. I wanted to stay in the hotel for a reason. Plus, it's not just about the money; it's about the experience and the convenience. I don't want to drive home after a rave, and I wanted to have some alone time with my boyfriend. Also, my friends aren't super close, but we've been cool in the past. I don't want to ruin that relationship by being too selfish. But at the same time, I need to take care of my own needs and plans. I guess I'm torn between being considerate of my friends' situation and sticking to my own plans and priorities. It's not easy to balance both, especially when it comes to money and personal space. Maybe I should think about what's more important to me: having that alone time with my boyfriend or helping out my friends. If I let them stay, I might feel guilty for not sticking to my original plan, but if I say no, I might feel guilty for being selfish. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Could I maybe suggest they find another place to stay or help them look for alternative options instead of letting them stay in my room? That way, I'm still being helpful without compromising my own plans. But then again, it's late, and they might not have time to find another place. Plus, I already have the room booked, and I don't want to feel like I'm wasting money if I don't use it. I think I need to prioritize my own needs and plans because I booked the room for a reason. It's important for me to have that time with my boyfriend, and I don't want to sacrifice that just to help my friends, especially since they made the choice not to book a room early. So, in the end, I think it's okay to say no because I have my own reasons for booking the room, and I need to take care of myself and my relationship. It's not selfish; it's just being responsible and true to my own needs.
